subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Alkyl group attached to benzene ring is?
explain: Alkyl groups donate electrons by hyperconjugation/induction, activating ring; direct o/p.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reactivity order of alkenes toward electrophilic addition?
explain: More alkyl groups on double bond increase electron density, increasing electrophilic addition rate.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Alkynes react with NaNH₂ to form?

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Anti-Markovnikov addition of water to alkene is achieved by?

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which product forms when ethyne reacts with HCl (1 mol)?

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In EAS, the rate-determining step is?

subject: Chemistry

explain: E⁺ addition to benzene forms arenium/σ-complex (Wheland intermediate); aromaticity restored by –H⁺.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Diels-Alder reaction requires a diene and a?

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hydrocarbon with formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (acyclic) belongs to which class?
explain: Acyclic alkynes have general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ due to two degrees of unsaturation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Dehydration of alcohols to give alkene follows which rule for major product?
explain: Saytzeff's rule: elimination gives the more substituted (stable) alkene as major product.

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

prompt: The C–C bond length order: alkane vs alkene vs alkyne (shortest to longest)?

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Dihedral angle between C–H bonds of adjacent carbons in eclipsed ethane?

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Dihedral angle between nearest H atoms on adjacent carbons in staggered ethane?
explain: Staggered: each rear H lies midway between two front H atoms, giving a 60° dihedral angle.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why is eclipsed ethane less stable than staggered?
explain: Eclipsed C–H bonds repel each other (torsional strain); bond angles stay about 109.5°.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In a Newman projection, the rear carbon is represented by:

subject: Chemistry
prompt: A Newman projection of ethane is obtained by viewing the molecule:

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Sawhorse projection of ethane shows the C–C bond viewed:
options: In the plane as a dash only
explain: Sawhorse: C–C drawn as a slanting line viewed obliquely, each carbon bearing three bonds.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ethane conformers cannot be separated at room temperature because:
options: C–C bond is a π bond
Rotation barrier is very low (~12 kJ/mol)

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Conformations of ethane arise due to rotation about which bond?
explain: Free rotation about the C–C single (σ) bond generates the different spatial arrangements.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Number of eclipsed and staggered maxima/minima in one full 360° rotation of ethane?
explain: The energy curve repeats every 120°, giving 3 eclipsed (maxima) and 3 staggered (minima) forms.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Conformers of ethane are classified as:
explain: Conformers have the same connectivity and differ only in spatial arrangement by rotation about single bonds.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In staggered ethane, the dihedral angle between H atoms on opposite sides (anti) is:
explain: Each H on the front carbon has an anti H on the rear carbon at 180°; the other two are at 60°.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Energy difference between eclipsed and staggered ethane is about:
explain: Eclipsed ethane is ~12.5 kJ/mol (≈3 kcal/mol) higher in energy than staggered; this is the torsional barrier.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Initiation step in photochemical chlorination of methane involves which process?

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which propagation step regenerates Cl• in the chlorination of methane?

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Trace ethane found in the chlorination of methane arises from which step?
explain: Two methyl radicals combine in a termination step to give C₂H₆.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Direct iodination of alkanes is reversible; which reagent is added to make it go forward?
explain: HI reduces R–I back to R–H. An oxidant like HIO₃ or HNO₃ removes HI by oxidising it to I₂.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Toluene with Cl₂/hν (or heat) gives mainly which product?
explain: Radical conditions give side-chain substitution via the resonance-stabilised benzyl radical. Ring chlorination needs Lewis acid.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: A trace of which species inhibits the radical chain chlorination of alkanes?
explain: O₂ traps alkyl radicals (forming peroxy radicals) and terminates chains, so there is an induction period.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: CH₄ and Cl₂ are mixed in the dark at room temperature. What happens?

explain: Cl• is needed to start the chain. Without light or heat, Cl₂ is not cleaved, so there is no reaction.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Vicinal dibromide on heating with Zn dust in ethanol gives:

subject: Chemistry
prompt: How many geometrical isomers does CH₃–CH=CH–CH=CH–CH₃ have?
explain: The molecule is symmetric, so there are EE, ZZ and EZ (= ZE), giving 3 isomers.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In the Z-isomer of an alkene, the higher CIP priority groups are:
explain: Z (zusammen) means the higher priority groups on each carbon lie on the same side of C=C.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Alkyl halide with alcoholic KOH gives alkene, but with aqueous KOH gives mainly:
explain: Aqueous KOH favours substitution (SN) to give the alcohol. Alcoholic KOH favours elimination.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Compared with trans-2-butene, cis-2-butene has a higher:

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which alkene is NOT capable of showing cis-trans isomerism?

subject: Chemistry
topic: Electrophilic addition: H2, X2, H2O, HX
prompt: Order of reactivity of hydrogen halides in electrophilic addition to alkenes?
explain: Acid strength and ease of H–X cleavage: HI > HBr > HCl > HF.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Electrophilic addition: H2, X2, H2O, HX
prompt: Order of heats of hydrogenation (ΔH, magnitude) of butene isomers?
explain: The more stable alkene releases less heat: trans-2-butene is the most stable, but-1-ene the least.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Electrophilic addition: H2, X2, H2O, HX
prompt: Br₂ addition to trans-but-2-ene (anti addition) gives which product?
explain: Anti addition to the trans alkene gives meso; the cis alkene gives the racemic mixture.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why does HCl not show the peroxide effect with propene?
options: H–Cl bond too strong; H abstraction endothermic
Cl• does not add to alkenes
Cl• is too stable to form

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In the peroxide effect on propene, which radical intermediate forms after Br• attack?
explain: Br• attacks the terminal carbon, giving the more stable 2° radical; this leads to the anti-Markovnikov product.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hydration of propene with dil. H₂SO₄ gives mainly?

subject: Chemistry
prompt: 2-Methylpropene + HBr in the presence of peroxide gives?
explain: The anti-Markovnikov product is (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Br, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane (isobutyl bromide).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which alkene gives the same product with HBr whether or not peroxide is present?
explain: A symmetrical alkene gives only one product (2-bromobutane) by either path.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Rate-determining step in electrophilic addition of HX to an alkene?
options: Attack of X⁻ on the carbocation
Loss of H⁺ from the product
explain: The slow step is protonation of C=C to give the carbocation; the attack of X⁻ is fast.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which pair of steps forms the propagation steps of the HBr peroxide addition?
options: Br₂ forms; Br₂ adds to alkene
R–O• adds to alkene; Br⁻ attacks
H• adds to alkene; Br• abstracts H
Br• adds to alkene; radical abstracts H from HBr
explain: The alkyl radical formed from Br• addition abstracts H from HBr, giving the product and regenerating Br•.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why does HI not show the peroxide effect with propene?
options: H–I bond is too strong to cleave
I• is too unreactive to add to C=C
I• adds only to give a 1° carbocation
explain: H–I is weak, but I• addition to C=C is endothermic; I• atoms simply combine to give I₂.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of an alkene: which reagent pair gives aldehydes/ketones without over-oxidation?
explain: Reductive workup (Zn/H₂O or Me₂S) stops at carbonyl compounds; H₂O₂ is oxidative.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis with oxidative workup (H₂O₂): an aldehyde fragment is converted to a…
explain: H₂O₂ oxidises RCHO to RCOOH; ketones remain unchanged.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Order of intermediates in ozonolysis of an alkene:
explain: Primary ozonide (molozonide) is unstable and rearranges to the secondary ozonide.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of propene (reductive workup) gives?
explain: CH₂= gives HCHO; CH₃CH= gives CH₃CHO.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of 2-methylpropene (reductive) gives?
explain: (CH₃)₂C= gives acetone; CH₂= gives HCHO.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene gives?
explain: Symmetric alkene with two (CH₃)₂C= ends gives 2 molecules of acetone.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of cyclohexene (reductive workup) gives?
explain: Ring opens; each alkene carbon becomes CHO: OHC(CH₂)₄CHO.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of cyclohexene with oxidative workup (H₂O₂) gives?
explain: Both CHO groups oxidise to COOH: HOOC(CH₂)₄COOH (adipic acid).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of 1-methylcyclohexene (reductive) gives?
explain: Ring opens to CH₃CO(CH₂)₄CHO, i.e. 6-oxoheptanal.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of buta-1,3-diene (reductive) gives HCHO and OHC–CHO in the ratio?
explain: CH₂=CH–CH=CH₂ → 2 HCHO + 1 glyoxal.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Main synthetic use of ozonolysis in structure determination of alkenes:
options: Count the number of H atoms
Locate the position of the C=C bond
explain: Carbonyl fragments reveal the carbons that were joined by the double bond.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Role of Zn dust in the reductive workup of ozonide:
explain: Zn destroys H₂O₂ formed on hydrolysis, so aldehydes aren't oxidised to acids.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Alkene C₅H₁₀ giving HCHO and butanone on reductive ozonolysis is?
explain: CH₂=C(CH₃)CH₂CH₃ gives HCHO + CH₃COCH₂CH₃.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of 2-methylbut-2-ene (reductive) gives?
explain: (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃ → (CH₃)₂C=O + CH₃CHO.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of styrene (C₆H₅CH=CH₂), reductive workup, gives?
explain: C₆H₅CH= gives C₆H₅CHO; CH₂= gives HCHO.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of but-1-ene (reductive) gives?
explain: CH₂=CH–CH₂CH₃ → HCHO + CH₃CH₂CHO.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Propene ozonolysis with H₂O₂ workup gives ethanoic acid and which other product?
explain: HCHO is oxidised to HCOOH and further to CO₂ + H₂O.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ethyne passed through a red-hot iron tube at 873 K mainly gives which product?
explain: Cyclic trimerisation of ethyne through a red-hot iron tube at 873 K gives benzene.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Low-density polythene is made from ethene by which type of mechanism?
explain: LDPE: ~1000–2000 atm, 350–570 K, traces of O₂ or peroxide; free radical addition.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: High-density polythene is prepared from ethene using which catalyst?
explain: Ziegler–Natta catalyst (TiCl₄ + triethylaluminium) gives linear HDPE at low pressure.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which monomer gives Teflon on polymerisation?
explain: Teflon is polytetrafluoroethene, made by addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Polyacrylonitrile (orlon) is formed by addition polymerisation of:
explain: Acrylonitrile (vinyl cyanide), CH₂=CHCN, is the monomer of PAN.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Industrial/lab preparation of ethyne: CaC₂ + 2H₂O gives ethyne and which other product?
explain: Hydrolysis of calcium carbide gives acetylene and slaked lime, Ca(OH)₂.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Vicinal dihalide on heating with alc. KOH (excess, then NaNH₂) mainly gives?
explain: Double dehydrohalogenation of vic- or gem-dihalides gives alkynes.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which reagent converts 1,2-dibromoethane to ethyne most effectively?
explain: Strong base NaNH₂ removes 2 HBr in two E2 steps to give alkyne.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Higher alkyne synthesis: RC≡C⁻Na⁺ reacts with R'X. Best choice of R'X?
explain: Alkynide is a strong base; 2°/3° halides give elimination, 1° gives SN2 substitution.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Alkynes: addition of H2, X2, H2O, HX
prompt: Hydroboration–oxidation (BH₃/THF, then H₂O₂/OH⁻) of a terminal alkyne gives?
explain: Anti-Markovnikov hydration gives an enol that tautomerises to the aldehyde RCH₂CHO.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Alkynes: addition of H2, X2, H2O, HX
prompt: Addition of HBr to propyne in presence of peroxide (1 mol) mainly gives?
explain: Peroxide effect (free radical) gives anti-Markovnikov product CH₃CH=CHBr.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Alkynes: addition of H2, X2, H2O, HX
prompt: Ni/Pt/Pd with excess H₂ converts an alkyne into?
explain: Unpoisoned metal catalysts cannot stop at alkene stage; complete reduction gives alkane.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Alkynes: addition of H2, X2, H2O, HX
prompt: Addition of 1 mol Br₂ to an alkyne in CCl₄ gives mainly which stereochemistry?
explain: Anti addition via bromonium ion gives the trans (E) 1,2-dibromoalkene.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Total number of σ bonds in a benzene molecule is:
explain: 6 C–C σ bonds + 6 C–H σ bonds = 12.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Cyclooctatetraene is non-aromatic mainly because it is:
explain: It has 8π e⁻ and adopts a tub shape, so conjugation is lost and it is non-aromatic.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The cyclopropenyl cation (C₃H₃⁺) is:
explain: It is planar and cyclic with 2π e⁻ (4n+2, n = 0), so it is aromatic.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Number of π electrons in naphthalene is:
explain: Five C=C in the Kekulé structure give 10π e⁻ (4n+2, n = 2), so it is aromatic.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Resonance energy of benzene is approximately:
explain: Resonance energy ≈ 150 kJ/mol (≈36 kcal/mol).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Different resonance structures of a molecule differ in the:
explain: Resonance structures keep the same atomic positions and differ only in the arrangement of electrons.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The cyclooctatetraene dianion (C₈H₈²⁻) is aromatic because it is planar with:
explain: Adding 2 e⁻ gives 10π e⁻ (4n+2, n = 2), so the ring becomes planar and aromatic.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why does benzene give only one 1,2-dibromo derivative, as Kekulé proposed?
options: Fixed alternate single and double bonds
explain: Kekulé suggested the double bonds oscillate, so the two 1,2-isomers interconvert and are one compound.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Order of stability for cyclic conjugated systems of similar size is:
explain: Aromaticity stabilises; anti-aromaticity destabilises relative to a non-aromatic analogue.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In nitrating mixture, the role of H₂SO₄ is to?
options: Act as a dehydrating agent only for benzene
explain: H₂SO₄ is the stronger acid; it protonates HNO₃, which loses H₂O to give NO₂⁺.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Further nitration of nitrobenzene (conc. HNO₃/H₂SO₄, heat) gives mainly?
explain: –NO₂ is a deactivating, meta-directing group, so the second NO₂ enters the meta position.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Direct iodination of benzene with I₂ needs which added reagent?
explain: I₂ is weakly electrophilic and HI formed is reversible; HNO₃ oxidises HI/I₂ to I⁺ and drives the reaction.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Benzene + excess Cl₂ in bright sunlight (no Lewis acid) gives?
explain: Under UV/sunlight, free-radical addition gives C₆H₆Cl₆ (gammexane), not substitution.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Phenol on treatment with conc. HNO₃ finally gives?
explain: –OH strongly activates o/p positions; conc. HNO₃ nitrates all three, giving picric acid.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Direct nitration of aniline with HNO₃/H₂SO₄ gives a considerable amount of which product?
explain: In strong acid, –NH₂ becomes –NH₃⁺, a meta director, so m-nitroaniline forms along with o/p.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which feature of Friedel-Crafts acylation is absent in alkylation?
explain: Acylium ion (RC≡O⁺) is resonance stabilised, so it does not rearrange.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why is Friedel-Crafts acylation product not further acylated?
explain: –COR is electron-withdrawing (–M), deactivating the ring; alkylation products are activated.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why does aniline fail to undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction?
explain: Basic N-lone pair attacks Lewis acid AlCl₃, giving a strongly deactivated ammonium-type salt.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The electrophile in Friedel-Crafts acylation with RCOCl/AlCl₃ is?
explain: AlCl₃ abstracts Cl⁻ from RCOCl to form the acylium ion.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Benzene + benzoyl chloride/anhyd. AlCl₃ gives?
explain: C₆H₅COCl gives C₆H₅COC₆H₅ (benzophenone).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Benzene + (CH₃)₃CCl/AlCl₃ gives which product?
explain: 3° carbocation is stable and attacks directly with no rearrangement.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which reagent can replace acyl chloride in Friedel-Crafts acylation?
explain: Acid anhydrides with AlCl₃ also generate the acylium ion.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which group is a meta director owing to –I and –M effects?
explain: –CHO withdraws electrons by –I and –M, deactivating ring and directing meta.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which is the strongest activating group for EAS in benzene?
explain: –NH₂ has strong +M; acylation of N or O reduces its lone pair donation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Acetylation of –NH₂ in aniline (to acetanilide) does what to activation?
explain: N lone pair is delocalised onto C=O, so +M is weaker; –NHCOCH₃ is still o/p.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which is a meta-directing group?
explain: –CCl₃ has strong –I from three Cl atoms with no +M/hyperconjugation, so it is meta directing.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which group is o/p directing and activates the ring through +M effect?
explain: –OCH₃ donates an O lone pair into the ring (+M); the others are meta directors.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which pair contains only meta directors?
explain: –COOH and –CN are –M/–I groups, meta directing, deactivating.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Least reactive towards EAS among these?
explain: –NO₂ is the strongest deactivator listed (–I, –M, strongest withdrawal).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which group is both activating and ortho/para directing but via –NHCOCH₃-type resonance?
explain: –NHCOCH₃ has N lone pair (+M), activating o/p; others are meta directors.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why does nitrobenzene fail to undergo Friedel–Crafts alkylation or acylation?
options: –NO₂ is an ortho/para director blocking attack
Steric hindrance by –NO₂ at all positions
Ring strongly deactivated by –M and –I of –NO₂
explain: –NO₂ withdraws electrons by –M and –I, so the ring is too deactivated for the weak carbocation/acylium electrophile.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Decarboxylation of RCOONa with soda lime gives an alkane with how many carbons relative to the acid?
explain: Soda lime removes CO₂ as Na₂CO₃, so the alkane has one carbon less than the acid salt.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In Kolbe electrolysis of aqueous sodium acetate, which gas is liberated at the cathode?
explain: Alkane and CO₂ form at the anode; water is reduced at the cathode to give H₂ and OH⁻.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Electrophilic addition: H2, X2, H2O, HX
prompt: Br₂/CCl₄ adds to cis-but-2-ene. Which product forms?
explain: Anti addition of Br₂ to the cis alkene gives (2R,3R) + (2S,3S), a racemic mixture. The trans alkene gives meso.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which monomer gives PVC on addition polymerisation?
explain: PVC (polyvinyl chloride) is formed from vinyl chloride, CH₂=CHCl.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Polystyrene is obtained by polymerisation of which monomer?
explain: Styrene (vinylbenzene), C₆H₅CH=CH₂, undergoes addition polymerisation to polystyrene.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Alkynes: addition of H2, X2, H2O, HX
prompt: In Hg²⁺/H₂SO₄ hydration of an alkyne, the unstable first-formed intermediate is a(n)?
explain: Markovnikov addition of water gives a vinyl alcohol (enol), which tautomerises to the more stable carbonyl compound.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which substituent on benzene is a meta director in EAS?
explain: The positively charged N has a strong –I effect and no lone pair, so it deactivates the ring and directs meta.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hydrolysis of aluminium carbide, Al₄C₃, with water gives which alkane?
explain: Al₄C₃ contains C⁴⁻ (methanide) ions, which on hydrolysis give CH₄.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: 1,4-Dibromobutane heated with Na in dry ether mainly gives:
explain: Intramolecular Wurtz coupling of an α,ω-dihalide forms a cycloalkane (a four-membered ring here).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Rate of dehydrohalogenation of R–X with alc. KOH to give alkene follows which order?
explain: Weaker C–X bond leaves more easily, so C–I breaks fastest and C–F slowest.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Compared with cis-but-2-ene, trans-but-2-ene has a higher:
explain: Trans is symmetrical and packs better in the crystal lattice, so it melts higher. Cis has the higher μ and b.p.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Electrophilic addition: H2, X2, H2O, HX
prompt: Stereochemistry of H₂ addition to an alkene over Pd/C or Pt surface?
explain: Both H atoms are delivered from the catalyst surface to the same face of the C=C, so addition is syn.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Styrene (C₆H₅CH=CH₂) + HBr, no peroxide, gives mainly?
explain: H adds to CH₂; the benzylic carbocation, stabilised by resonance, gives PhCH(Br)CH₃.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: 1-Methylcyclohexene + HBr (no peroxide) gives mainly?
explain: H adds to the C with more H (C-2), forming a 3° carbocation at C-1; Br⁻ then attacks it.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In the peroxide effect, which radical abstracts H from HBr in the initiation step?
explain: Peroxide homolysis gives RO•, which abstracts H from HBr to generate Br•.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Order of stability of alkyl free radicals (relevant to the peroxide effect)?
explain: Hyperconjugation stabilises radicals as it does carbocations, so more alkyl groups mean a more stable radical.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The six π electrons of benzene are best described as:
options: Held by alternate carbon atoms only
explain: Six p orbitals overlap sideways to give a delocalised π cloud above and below the ring plane.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In EAS of nitrobenzene, o/p attack is disfavoured because the σ-complex has +ve charge on?
explain: o/p attack puts + charge on the C attached to –NO₂, which is very unstable; meta attack avoids this.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene (reductive workup) gives?
explain: Ring opens at C=C: CH₃CO–(CH₂)₄–COCH₃, which is octane-2,7-dione.
